label: USE CASE 21
title: How Wake Words Like 'Hey Siri' Work

scenes.text: You say, hey Google, from across the room, and your phone lights up instantly. [1] Is it recording everything you say, all day? [2] Let's break down how wake word detection really works.

Here's the flow. [1] The microphone listens in short, rolling slices of about one second. [2] A tiny model on the device checks each slice for the wake word. [3] If the score crosses a threshold, it wakes up. [4] Only then does the full assistant start recording your request, [5] and send it for speech to text, and the AI brain.

[1] This is called keyword spotting. [2] The model is trained on thousands of people saying the wake word, [3] in different accents, and noisy rooms, [4] plus lots of audio that is not the wake word, so it learns the difference.

data.definition: A tiny always-on model that listens for one specific phrase and ignores everything else.

scenes.text: Why a tiny model? [1] It runs all day, so it must use very little battery. Some phones use a special low power chip just for this. [2] It must respond in a fraction of a second. [3] And it runs on the device, so your everyday talk isn't sent anywhere.

There are two kinds of mistakes. [1] A false wake, when a TV show says something similar, and the assistant turns on by accident. [2] A missed wake, when you say it, and nothing happens. [3] The threshold balances these two.

left.title: False wake
left.label: wakes up when you didn't call

scenes.text: Here are four terms. [1] Wake word, the trigger phrase. [2] Threshold, the score needed to wake. [3] Voice match, extra checking that it's your voice. [4] And false accept rate, how often it wakes by mistake.

Here's a common myth. [1] People think the assistant records and uploads everything, all day. [2] The wake word check happens on the device. Audio is usually sent only after it wakes. But false wakes can send short clips, so check your privacy settings.

data.myth: The assistant uploads everything you say, all day.
data.fact: The wake check runs on the device. Audio is usually sent only after waking, but false wakes can send clips.

scenes.text: Quick quiz! Where does the wake word check usually happen? [1] Pause and think, and if you get it right, comment below! <pause 3.2> [2] On the device itself, with a tiny low power model!

Let's recap. [1] A tiny model listens in short slices, on the device. [2] It's trained on many voices, and lots of non-wake-word audio. [3] A threshold balances false wakes and missed wakes.
